raw_response:
Let me think through this like a real farmer would.

---

**My thinking for this year:**

Well, I've been doing this wheat-maize rotation on my 30.4 mu for 30 years now. I'm 48, got primary school education. My family has 5 mouths — wife, me, and the kids, though some work in town now. That off-farm money helps, but the farm is still what feeds us and pays for the kids' schooling.

**Winter wheat:** I plant every year around October 5th to 15th, right after the National Day holiday. This year I'll do the same — my father taught me that window, and 30 years says don't mess with it. I use an improved wheat variety, whatever the seed shop has that's doing well. Last year I paid about 90 yuan per mu for seed. I plant about 15-16 kg of seed per mu.

For fertilizer, my neighbor Lao Wang — he's got a bit more education — he told me he uses about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu total, split between base and topdress. I've always done around 15-18 kg, and it works. I'll put down compound fertilizer as base (roughly 50 kg of the 15-15-15 stuff per mu, which gives me some N, P, K), then topdress with urea at jointing if the wheat looks good. That's two applications. I know some big farms do three, but that's too fancy for me.

I'll irrigate 3 times: once before winter to help establishment, once at green-up in spring, and once at flowering. The well water costs money — pumping isn't free — but skipping irrigation on wheat is too risky. I remember 2009 when I tried to save on water, the yield dropped bad. Better to spend the money.

I expect around 450 kg per mu for wheat if the weather is normal. Last year I got about 430 kg, so 450 is reasonable.

**Summer maize:** This is the hard part. I harvest wheat around June 10-15, and I need that maize in the ground within days — sometimes I plant the same day we cut wheat. No time for fancy tillage. I usually do minimal tillage or just plant right into the stubble. I hire a custom planter sometimes because my old tractor can't handle the rush.

Maize seed — I always buy hybrid seed fresh. Can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't work. Costs about 70 yuan per mu. Plant around mid-June, harvest late September.

For maize fertilizer, I usually put down less than wheat. Maybe 12-15 kg N per mu. I can do one application at planting with compound fertilizer, and if the rains are good, that's often enough. Sometimes I add a bit at the big-flush stage if I see it needs it.

Maize irrigation — I usually do 1-2 times. If the summer rains come regular, maybe just once at the critical stage. If it's dry like 2022, twice. Groundwater is getting expensive, so I watch the sky.

I expect about 500 kg per mu for maize. Last year was 480, but the year before was 520. Let's say 500.

**Labor:** My wife and I do most work. During wheat harvest and maize planting, those 3-4 days are hell — we work 14 hours a day. I usually hire 2-3 days of labor for harvest and another 2-3 days for planting the maize, because the window is so tight. Family puts in maybe 25 days per crop, hired about 3-4 days per crop.

**Costs:** Seed, fertilizer, irrigation pumping, pesticide — wheat needs herbicide and maybe one insecticide spray. Maize usually needs herbicide. Total costs per mu... wheat is about 380-400 yuan, maize about 320-350 yuan. For 30.4 mu, total input costs around 21,500-22,000 yuan for the year.

I worry about fertilizer prices going up. Last year urea was expensive. But I'm not going to cut back too much — losing yield hurts more than saving on fertilizer. That's the lesson 30 years taught me.
